unsupported_claims: DeepWalk has no built-in edge-cutoff threshold (the paper says different cutoff thresholds are tried to convert the network into a binary network, so a threshold is applied in the experiment)
If a threshold sweep were run, removing every edge would leave embedding quality at chance (not reported in the evidence; speculative)
rationale: The answer correctly rejects the false premise that removing all edges gives DeepWalk's best threshold, and notes that the optimum retains edges, which matches the paper's statement that the best performance is achieved when all edges are kept. However, it wrongly claims DeepWalk has no cutoff threshold, contrary to the paper's description of trying different cutoffs, and adds an unsupported speculation about chance-level performance.
